2608.08164.title: STEMMA: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Self-Identity Consistency in LLMs
2608.08164.paper_summary: Knowledge Distillation is a widely adopted technique in the training and fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) enabling transfer of structured information and functional behavior from a large teacher model to a smaller student model while significantly reducing computational costs. However, as the use of distillation increases in both scale and complexity it raises an important question about what kind of knowledge is really transferred from the teacher model. In this work, we argue that apart from the functional knowledge, student models also learn behavioral patterns, specifically how a model represents its own identity raising concerns about output homogeneity, model biases, and accountability. To address this challenge, we introduce STEMMA, a multi-modal and multi-agent framework in which role specific agents collaboratively probe self identification behavior in different models. We also contribute a set of adversarial prompts designed manually to evaluate identity consistency in LLMs. Our results show that to an extent most models are vulnerable to inconsistencies in self-representations.
2608.08164.paper_summary_zh: 知識蒸餾是一種廣泛採用的技術，用於大型語言模型（LLMs）的訓練和微調，能夠將結構化信息和功能行為從大型教師模型轉移到較小的學生模型，同時顯著降低計算成本。<lb/>然而，隨著蒸餾在規模和複雜性上的使用增加，這引發了一個重要問題，即從教師模型實際轉移了什麼樣的知識。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們主張，除了功能性知識外，學生模型還學習行為模式，特別是模型如何表現其自身身份，這引發了關於輸出同質性、模型偏見和問責制的擔憂。<lb/>為了解決這一挑戰，我們引入了STEMMA，一個多模態和多代理框架，其中角色特定的代理協同探測不同模型中的自我識別行為。<lb/>我們還貢獻了一組手動設計的對抗性提示，旨在評估LLMs中的身份一致性。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，在某種程度上，大多數模型對自我表現的不一致性是脆弱的。
